paper.title_en: Gravitational wave signatures and forecasts in f(Q, T) modified gravity
paper.abstract_en: Recent developments in Gravitational-Wave (GW) astronomy offer a powerful and independent probe of gravity beyond General Relativity (GR). In this work, we study the Gravitational-Wave and cosmological implications of f(Q, T) gravity, a modified theory in which the gravitational action depends on the non-metricity scalar Q and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor T. We derive the gravitational wave propagation equation within the considered separable f(Q, T) framework and obtain the corresponding modified GW luminosity distance induced by the altered cosmological background evolution. We consider two representative functional forms of f(Q, T) and constrain their parameters using mock GW standard-siren datasets corresponding to current (LIGO-Virgo), space-based (LISA), and next-generation (Einstein Telescope) detectors. We use simulated Gravitational-Wave standard-siren catalogs corresponding to LISA, LIGO-Virgo, and the Einstein Telescope to investigate the prospective sensitivity of these observations to the model parameters. The analysis is formulated as a forecast study based on a fiducial $\Lambda $CDM mock cosmology. We emphasize that the resulting parameter estimates are sensitivity indicators for the adopted mock realization rather than definitive observational prospective constraints. Our results show that the increasing number of standard sirens, particularly for an ET-like catalog, substantially improves the sensitivity to the background cosmological parameters, while significant degeneracies remain among the parameters describing the non-metricity sector and the matter-geometry coupling. This highlights the strong potential of next-generation GW cosmology to test the fundamental nature of gravity and assess the viability of f(Q, T) gravity.
